papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $\omega_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $\omega_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $\omega_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $\omega_\mathbb{F}$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.

papers.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
papers.abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.

papers.title: $\delta$-superderivations of simple finite-dimensional Jordan and Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of a $\delta$-superderivation of a superalgebra. $\delta$-Derivations of Cartan-type Lie superalgebras are treated, as well as $\delta$-superderivations of simple finite-dimensional Lie superalgebras and Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. We give a complete description of $\{1}{2}$-derivations for Cartan-type Lie superalgebras. It is proved that nontrivial $\delta$-(super)derivations are missing on the given classes of superalgebras, and as a consequence, $\delta$-superderivations are shown to be trivial on simple finite-dimensional noncommutative Jordan superalgebras of degree at least 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Also we consider $\delta$-derivations of unital flexible and semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan algebras over a field of characteristic not 2.

papers.title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
papers.abstract: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

papers.title: Central series of cocommutative Hopf braces
papers.abstract: By extending some classical results known for groups and skew braces, we define and investigate central series of cocommutative Hopf braces. Both left and right central series are defined using a $\star$-product that measures the difference between the two algebra operations, and naturally leads to introducing the notions of socle and of annihilator of a cocommutative Hopf brace. We characterize the central extensions relative to the subcategories of cocommutative Hopf algebras and of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras, respectively. Since the category of cocommutative Hopf braces is semi-abelian and it has enough projectives with respect to the class of cleft extensions, one can then establish suitable Hopf formulae for their homology. These are expressed in terms of the corresponding notions of relative commutators of cocommutative Hopf braces. In particular, the one relative to the subcategory of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras turns out to be the Huq commutator.

papers.title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
papers.abstract: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.

papers.title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings
papers.abstract: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.

papers.title: Normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras and Landau-Lifshitz type of equations
papers.abstract: We present normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras with dihedral symmetry of order 4, which arise naturally in the context of Landau-Lifshitz type of equations. These normal forms provide a transparent description and allow a classification of such Lie algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Using this perspective, we show that a Lie algebra introduced by Uglov, as well as the hidden symmetry algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation introduced by Holod, can each be realised as an elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra. Furthermore, we realise the Wahlquist-Estabrook algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation in terms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras. This construction reveals that, as a complex Lie algebra, it is isomorphic to the direct sum of an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra and the two-dimensional abelian Lie algebra $\mathbb{C}^2$. Finally, we apply the automorphic Lie algebra framework to an $n$-component generalisation of the Landau-Lifshitz equation due to Golubchik and Sokolov in the case $n=3$.

papers.title: Noncommutative principal bundles and central extensions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical theory of spin structures, we develop a theory for lifting free C$^*$-dynamical systems, a.k.a. noncommutative principal bundles, along central extensions. This theory extends the bundle-theoretic notion of spin structures and yields a complete existence and classification result for such lifts. Using factor system techniques and Picard formalism, our approach introduces new invariants and obstruction classes, thereby unifying geometric, cohomological, and operator-algebraic perspectives. A range of examples demonstrates the scope of the theory.

papers.title: Algebras with bounded multiplicities of the central cocharacters
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an associative PI-algebra over a field of characteristic zero. The central polynomials of $A$ give rise to a sequence $\{\chi_n^z(A)\}_{n\geq 1}$ of $S_n$-characters, called its central cocharacters. A natural problem is to understand which algebraic properties of $A$ are imposed by bounds on the multiplicities occurring in the decompositions of these cocharacters into irreducible characters. We prove that these multiplicities are bounded by one if and only if there exist scalars $(\alpha,\beta)\neq(0,0)$ such that $\alpha[x_1,x_2]x_1+\beta x_1[x_1,x_2]$ takes values in the center of $A$. This provides a central analogue of the Ananin-Kemer theorem for ordinary cocharacters. We also characterize the algebras whose central cocharacter multiplicities are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Ramified convolution and monodromy bases for symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We realize the positive enveloping algebra of a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra by convolution on a ramified preprojective species over $\mathbb{C}((t))$. The coefficients are alternating traces of tame monodromy on representation flag varieties. We prove the relative Serre relations modulo classes induced from proper finite extensions. Monodromy evaluations at compatible generic points of the central reductions yield an integral basis respecting the top and socle crystals. The basis is unchanged by scaling the symmetrizer, induces bases of integrable representation lattices, and agrees with Lusztig's semicanonical basis when the Cartan matrix is symmetric. We prove the acyclic convolution conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer for all symmetrizable Cartan matrices and all positive integral symmetrizers. Finally, we give a counterexample to the Support Conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer and compute a ramified lift for which monodromy restores the Serre relation.

papers.title: A sharp weighted commutator inequality for rank-one matrices
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be positive definite Hermitian, where $n\ge 2$, and define $\|X\|_A^2=\mathrm{tr}(AX^*X)$ for all $X\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$. We determine the smallest constant $C_A$ for which $$ \|XY-YX\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le C_A\|X\|_A^2\|Y\|_A^2 $$ holds for all rank-one $X,Y\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. The constant depends only on the two smallest eigenvalues of $A$ and is determined by a strictly monotone scalar equation. This answers the sharp-constant question for rank-one matrices formulated by Fang and Cheng. We also characterize all equality pairs.

papers.title: Continuous spectrum-shrinking maps between finite-dimensional power-associative algebras
papers.abstract: For finite-dimensional complex power-associative algebras $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, each equipped with its unique Hausdorff vector topology, we characterize continuous spectrum-shrinking maps $\phi:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}$, i.e. maps satisfying $\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{B}}(\phi(x)) \subseteq\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$. The spectrum of an element is the zero set of its minimal polynomial, computed in the unitization for nonunital algebras. No such map exists when $\mathcal{A}$ is unital and $\mathcal{B}$ is nonunital. Otherwise, we symmetrize both products by setting $x\circ y:=\tfrac{1}{2}(xy+yx)$ and factor out the nilradicals to obtain semisimple Jordan quotients. We prove that a continuous map $\phi$ is spectrum-shrinking precisely when, for every $x\in\mathcal{A}$, Jacobson's generic minimal polynomials of the simple quotient coordinates of $\phi(x)$ are products of fixed nonnegative integer powers of those of $x$, with an additional fixed monomial factor allowed when $\mathcal{A}$ is nonunital. Comparing degrees gives linear Diophantine equations characterizing existence, and every nonnegative integer solution is realized by a polynomial spectrum-shrinking map. Spectrum preservation, meaning equality of spectra, is equivalent to additional positivity conditions. We also determine when every continuous spectrum-shrinking map preserves spectra and show that every continuous map $f:\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $f(x)\in\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear and satisfies $f(x\circ y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal{A}$.

papers.title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
papers.abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincar\'e polynomial is nonzero.

papers.title: Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers
papers.abstract: Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case. As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian \v{C}ech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $\Lambda_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partial\Lambda_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question remains open. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $\Lambda_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: Near-Rings and Skew Braces
papers.abstract: This paper provides a deeper analysis of Rump's correspondence between near-rings and skew braces. We show that, under a topological assumption on the structure of a near-ring, Rump's correspondence is invertible and it is always possible to construct an associated skew brace. Furthermore, we provide several examples where this topological assumption is fulfilled in well-known algebraic structures such as the Nottingham group, groups of triangular functions, iterated wreath products of arbitrary groups, and groups of IA-automorphisms of free nilpotent groups.

papers.title: $\delta$-derivations of classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We consider the $\delta$-derivations of classical Lie superalgebras and prove that these superalgebras admit nonzero $\delta$-derivations only when $\delta = 0,1/2,1$. The structure of $1/2$-derivations for classical Lie superalgebras is completely determined.

papers.title: On $\delta$-superderivations of simple superalgebras of Jordan brackets
papers.abstract: A complete description of $\delta$-derivations and $\delta$-superderivations is given for simple unital superalgebras of Jordan brackets over a field of characteristic different from~$2$ \textup{(}and, for the odd $\delta$-superderivations, different from~$3$; see Remark~A for characteristic~$3$\textup{)} and for simple unital finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\neq2$ \textup{(}with the corrections of Remarks~A and~C for $p>2$\textup{)}. As a consequence, a criterion for simple unital superalgebras of Jordan brackets to be special is obtained.

papers.title: Commutative algebras satisfying univariate identities with vanishing Peirce polynomial
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies $(2,3)$-palintropic algebras, a class of commutative algebras defined by the identity $(x^{2})^3 - (x^{3})^2 = 0$. This specific relation is the simplest generator of the $2$-dimensional space of minimal-degree evanescent identities in degree $6$, and encompasses several well-studied structures, including Jordan and medial algebras. The primary motivation for investigating these algebras lies in their trivial Peirce polynomials, which removes a priori restrictions on the spectrum of the multiplication operator associated with an idempotent. This paper reviews and further develops the theory of Peirce operators, Peirce polynomials, and second-order linearizations. It shows that despite the triviality of the Peirce polynomial, any idempotent $c$ admits well-behaved, explicit fusion rules for multiplication between its $\lambda$-Peirce spaces for $\lambda \neq \tfrac{1}{2}$. Furthermore, multiplication by a nonsingular idempotent is an algebra homomorphism. Finally, there are given concrete examples of $(2,3)$-palintropic algebras, together with applications of these algebraic structures to commutative polynomial maps.

papers.title: Regular Sublattices, O Closed Ideals and Dedekind MacNeille Completions
papers.abstract: We study regular sublattices of lattices that satisfy the Join-Infinite Distributive Law (JID) under Dedekind MacNeille completion. Using order convergence, we identify the lattice of O-closed ideals with Crawleys completion, and compare it with the Dedekind MacNeille completion. When DM(L) satisfies (JID), this comparison yields extension results for lattice homomorphisms. In particular, if Y is a regular sublattice of a complete lattice L, and L and DM(Y) satisfy (JID), then the canonical extension lattice-embeds DM(Y) into L with join-regular image. We also give a sharp finite-dimensional obstruction: there exists an infinitely distributive regular sublattice of R3 whose Dedekind MacNeille completion is not distributive, and therefore cannot be lattice embedded in R3. In contrast, we prove that the inclusion of every join-regular sublattice of R2 with a least and a greatest element extends canonically to a lattice embedding of its MacNeille completion into R2.
